key_insight: Seer improves small deep-research agents by using shared learned models to predict and score candidate actions before executing only the selected action.
engineering_relevance: Reusable inference-time guidance can strengthen locally run agents without agent-specific retraining or tool calls for discarded candidates, at the cost of extra local inference.
method: Train a tool-response simulator offline on real research call–response pairs.
Train a value estimator on research histories labeled with discounted terminal correctness.
Predict and score candidate outcomes; commit only the selected action and its real tool response to history.
evidence_signal: Across multiple deep-research benchmarks, Seer improves different language models; GAIA accuracy rises from 13.6% to 41.7% for Qwen3.5-4B and from 22.3% to 50.5% for Qwen3.5-9B.
watch_item: Simulation and scoring errors limit gains from wider candidate search, while added inference creates a compute trade-off on constrained devices.
paper_title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
